hypothesis_card.mechanism: AWS administers spot prices per instance family with slow, persistent repricing cycles (capacity build-outs, generation transitions); the 730-day pooled change distribution is stationary by construction and carries zero trend information, so during a family-level repricing cycle every quantile is biased in the drift direction. Adding clip(family median 90-day log change, +/-0.5) * 0.15 to the h90 quantiles shifts the center and both tails with the cycle; blending the series' own 730-day change quantiles with the family pool (w=0.3 h90 / 0.5 h180) lets AZ-specific administered paths (which differ from the family pool: e.g. use2-az1 starting 2024-01) sharpen the long-horizon center where the family pool over-disperses. Both levers are unconditional within their horizon gates (no validation-selected firing), point-in-time (trailing windows only), and bounded (clip +/-0.5 log trend, +/-1.5 log final quantiles).
hypothesis_card.expected_observation: Discovery: pooled 0.2675 -> ~0.271 (+0.0035), h90 0.2377 -> 0.2467 (+0.009), h180 +0.0006, h30 exactly unchanged (trend gated off after the h30 variant measured -0.017), median +0.003, coverage -0.004 (0.664 -> 0.660, still inside the gate-3 band given the champion's +0.09 Discovery->Holdout coverage gap). Dense 16-origin monthly backtest: pooled delta +0.0035 (h90 +0.0081, h180 +0.0011, h30 0.0), 62.5% of origins improved, worst single series -0.0025 pooled contribution. Holdout: pooled ~0.292 vs gate-1 threshold 0.2916 (champion 0.2886 + 0.003), median ~0.274, coverage ~0.75.
hypothesis_card.competing_explanation: The rival explanation of the same errors: the gain is not family-trend information but a generic center shift toward recent levels that happens to help in the 2023-24 window where family levels moved persistently in one direction; under it, the h90 gain should appear equally at h30 and h180 (any horizon-consistent drift shift would score), and it should vanish in a sideways regime. Evidence against: the same shift at h30 was Discovery-NEGATIVE (-0.017, dry run 1) and at h180 loss-negative (-0.033 on pseudo-origins) while positive at h90 — a generic center shift would have helped all three; and the per-series blend component is horizon-gated (w=0 at h30) yet still positive, which a pure drift artifact cannot explain.
hypothesis_card.test: Paired dry run on the 16 Discovery origins vs the champion (pooled +0.0035, h90 +0.0091 / h180 +0.0006 / h30 0.0 exactly, 11/16 origins improved, screen PASS) plus a dense 16-origin monthly backtest (pooled delta +0.0035, h90 +0.0081, h180 +0.0011, 62.5% origins improved, worst series contribution -0.0025). The h30 gate was decided by dry run 1 (trend at h30: -0.0169 skill, reverted) and the h180 gate by the pseudo-origin scan (trend at h180: -0.033 skill, gated off before any dry run).
hypothesis_card.rejection_condition: Rejected if Discovery pooled <= 0.2675 (final: 0.2710, screen PASS) or sanity fails (none). The drift-shift mechanism is falsified if the Holdout h90 skill <= 0.2226 (champion's) or the pooled gain over the champion is < +0.001 (noise); the per-series blend is falsified if the h180 skill <= 0.3870 (champion's). Gate-3 risk: if Holdout coverage falls below 0.70 the h90 tail shift over-corrected and the trend weight must drop to 0.10 or the shift must be applied to q50 only.

hypothesis: The champion's 44.9% q50 loss share at 30/90/180-day horizons is family-level directional drift that its 730-day pooled family change-quantiles cannot represent: p4d (A100) prices rose through 2023-24 (66% q90 breach at h180) while p5 (H100) prices fell (48% q10 breach at h90). Two pack-only levers fix part of it: (1) a per-series x family change-quantile blend (w=0.3 at h90, w=0.5 at h180, own path >= 30 pairs) uses each AZ's own administered price path, which is more informative than the family pool at long horizons; (2) a family recent-trend drift shift (median 90-day family log change, clip +/- 0.5, x 0.15) added to all three quantiles at h90 only — h30 measured Discovery-negative (-0.017) and h180 loss-negative (-0.033 on pseudo-origins), both gated off. Exogenous news signals were re-tested point-in-time and returned nothing usable (third falsification); no external signal is used.
market_insight: The forecast assumes AWS GPU spot prices at 30-180-day horizons are driven by (a) family-level administered repricing that persists for months — p4d/A100 capacity was repriced upward through 2023-24 as legacy supply tightened (NextPlatform 2023-07-27 H100 instance pricing analysis; HPCwire 2023-11-08 "H100 capacity increasing, prices could get cheaper") while p5/H100 spot rates drifted down as supply eased (TechSpot 2024-02-27, techspot.com/news/102049: buyers selling surplus hardware as constraints ease) — and (b) AZ-level deviations that revert toward the family median because AWS compresses spot discounts and rebalances reclaimed capacity (AWS News Blog 2023-10-31, aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/announcing-amazon-ec2-capacity-blocks-for-ml; zenn.dev re:Invent 2024 recap: "significant drop [in Spot prices] over the past year... continue to look for ways to lower these prices further"). The committed levers encode exactly these two drivers from the pack itself: the family 90-day trend shift (h90) captures (a), the per-series blend and the iter-1 below-median up-shift capture (b). Dated counter-evidence recorded: aggregate news direction is unusable — CostPulse 2024-08-02 (costpulse.io/aws-price-changes/amazon-elastic-compute-cloud/20240802172840) logged 65,388 cuts AND 259,823 increases on the same day, so no news-drift gate is used (third falsification). The view would change if AWS stopped compressing spot discounts (broad spot increases leaving below-median AZs persistently cheap), if a new generation (p6/Blackwell) made p4d/p5 structurally obsolete and monotonically cheaper, or if the h90 trend gain failed to transfer to the 2025 Holdout window.
bottleneck: Ideas/data: the analysis budget (6) was consumed mostly by debugging my own pseudo-origin harness (a level-vs-change scoring bug produced champion skill -2.86 and would have falsified every lever); the pack itself lacks exogenous tables (daily_statistics/aggregator_medians/index_prints are empty) and news is direction-mixed (CostPulse 2024-08-02: 65,388 cuts AND 259,823 increases the same day), so regime information had to be extracted from series_history alone.
